title: Fppf descent data of algebraic spaces realized as sheaves
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use the universes and site skeletons of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic spaces over $S$ are fppf sheaves with the atlas and diagonal conditions of [def-trf-algebraic-space]; their morphisms are natural transformations. Let $X$ and $X_i$ be algebraic spaces over $S$, indexed by a set $I$, and let $a_i:X_i\to X$ be flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], jointly surjective on field-valued point classes [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. This is an fppf covering of algebraic spaces. Let $\mathcal D$ have objects algebraic spaces $V_i\to X_i$ with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_X X_j\xrightarrow{\sim}X_i\times_X V_j$ over $X_i\times_X X_j$ satisfying the triple-overlap cocycle $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}$ after pullback, and arrows the families of $X_i$-morphisms commuting with these isomorphisms. Let $\mathcal L$ be the full subcategory of fppf sheaves of sets $F$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], endowed with a map $F\to X$, for which each sheaf pullback $X_i\times_X F$ is an algebraic space. Sheaf pullbacks are computed by pairs of sections with equal images. The functor $\mathcal L\to\mathcal D$ sending $F$ to the pullbacks $X_i\times_X F$ and their canonical overlap isomorphisms is an equivalence. In particular every datum has a sheaf realization with displayed local isomorphisms inducing exactly $\varphi_{ij}$, and maps between two such sheaves over $X$ correspond bijectively to compatible families of maps over the $X_i$. No algebraicity assertion about $F$ itself is included.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), equivalence and clause (1); algebraic-space fppf coverings: spaces-topologies.tex definition-fppf-covering.

proof.text: For $F\to X$ in $\mathcal L$, put $V_i=X_i\times_XF$. The canonical overlap map sends $((x_i,f),x_j)$ to $(x_i,(x_j,f))$. These are morphisms of algebraic spaces because morphisms are natural transformations; the overlap fibre products exist by the cited fibre-product lemma. On a triple overlap both composites keep the same $f$ and reorder the same three base coordinates, proving the cocycle. A map $F\to G$ acts on the $f$ coordinate, so this construction is a functor $R:\mathcal L\to\mathcal D$.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), coequalizer construction and verification of the quasi-inverses

proof.text: Every section $x\in X(T)$, for an $S$-scheme $T$, locally lifts to some $X_i$. Indeed, $Y_i=T\times_X X_i$ are algebraic spaces by the fibre-product lemma and form an fppf family over $T$ by covering calculus (2). Choose the surjective etale scheme atlas $U_i\to Y_i$ supplied by the definition of algebraic space. Covering calculus (1) and (3) show that the composites $U_i\to T$ form an fppf family; (4) identifies it as a covering of schemes in the given site. Their maps to $X_i$ lift $x$. This proves the local lifting needed below without assuming any $X_i\to X$ representable.

For a datum $(V_i,\varphi_{ij})$, write $b_i:V_i\to X_i$. For sections $x_i\in X_i(T)$ and $x_j\in X_j(T)$ over the same $x\in X(T)$, define $\tau_{ij}(x_i,x_j)$ on the fibre of $V_i(T)\to X_i(T)$ by the $V_j$ coordinate of $\varphi_{ij}(v_i,x_j)$. The cocycle gives $\tau_{ik}=\tau_{jk}\tau_{ij}$, with the appropriate three fixed coordinates. On repeated coordinates $\tau_{ii}^2=\tau_{ii}$; since it is bijective it is the identity. Taking the triple $(i,j,i)$ gives $\tau_{ji}=\tau_{ij}^{-1}$. Thus on $A(T)=\coprod_iV_i(T)$ the rule $(i,v_i)\sim(j,v_j)$ iff their images in $X(T)$ agree and $v_j=\tau_{ij}(b_i(v_i),b_j(v_j))(v_i)$ is an equivalence relation. Naturality of the $\varphi_{ij}$ makes it stable under restriction. Define the quotient presheaf $P(T)=A(T)/{\sim}$ with its induced map $P\to X$. This is the pointwise quotient underlying the coequalizer of Tag 0ADT.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), coequalizer construction and verification of the quasi-inverses

proof.text: Take $F=P^{++}$ with unit $\eta:P\to F$. The cited plus theorem supplies an actual sheaf and its sheafification universal property in the chosen universe containing the site and the set $I$; thus no colimit over a large category is used. Since $X$ is a sheaf, $P\to X$ extends uniquely to $p:F\to X$. For each $i$ define $q_i:V_i\to F$ by $v\mapsto\eta([i,v])$ and $\theta_i:V_i\to X_i\times_XF$ by $v\mapsto(b_i(v),q_i(v))$. These are natural transformations over $X_i$.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), coequalizer construction and verification of the quasi-inverses

proof.text: The maps $\theta_i$ are injective on sections. If $\theta_i(v)=\theta_i(w)$ over $T$, then $b_i(v)=b_i(w)$ and $\eta([i,v])=\eta([i,w])$. The local-equality clause of the cited sheafification lemma gives a covering on which $[i,v]=[i,w]$ in $P$. By the quotient relation from step 3 and $\tau_{ii}(x_i,x_i)=1$, this says $v=w$ there. Since $V_i$ is a sheaf, equality on that covering implies $v=w$ over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), coequalizer construction and verification of the quasi-inverses

proof.text: Each $\theta_i$ is also surjective on sections. Given $(x_i,f)\in(X_i\times_XF)(T)$, the local-representation clause of the cited lemma gives a covering $T_a\to T$ on which $f=\eta([j_a,v_a])$. Write $x_{j_a}=b_{j_a}(v_a)$. The equality defining the pullback says $a_i(x_i)=a_{j_a}(x_{j_a})$, so put $w_a=\tau_{j_ai}(x_{j_a},x_i)(v_a)\in V_i(T_a)$. The quotient relation gives $\theta_i(w_a)=(x_i,f)|_{T_a}$. On pairwise overlaps these $w_a$ have equal images under $\theta_i$ and are equal by step 5. The sheaf axiom glues them uniquely to $w\in V_i(T)$ with $\theta_i(w)=(x_i,f)$. Consequently the $\theta_i$ are isomorphisms, with inverse the unique preimage on every $T$, natural since $\theta_i$ is natural. Hence $F$ lies in $\mathcal L$.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), coequalizer construction and verification of the quasi-inverses

proof.text: The displayed isomorphisms recover the original transitions, rather than just isomorphic local objects: for $(v_i,x_j)$ the definition of the quotient gives $q_i(v_i)=q_j(\tau_{ij}(b_i(v_i),x_j)(v_i))$. Therefore the canonical reordering overlap map for $F$, expressed via $\theta_i$ and $\theta_j$, is precisely $\varphi_{ij}$. If $h_i:V_i\to W_i$ is an arrow of data, its compatibility is the equality $h_j\tau_{ij}=\sigma_{ij}h_i$. It therefore induces $P_V\to P_W$, $[i,v]\mapsto[i,h_i(v)]$. The universal property of sheafification extends this to a unique $F_V\to F_W$. It is over $X$ because the two maps to $X$ agree on $P_V$. Uniqueness also proves preservation of identities and composition. This defines a functor $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal L$, and the $\theta_i$ give a natural isomorphism from the identity datum to $RQ$.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), coequalizer construction and verification of the quasi-inverses

proof.text: For $G\to X$ in $\mathcal L$, apply $Q$ to its canonical datum $V_i=X_i\times_XG$. Forgetting $x_i$ gives $P(T)\to G(T)$, $[i,(x_i,g)]\mapsto g$. It is well defined because the canonical transitions leave $g$ fixed, and it extends to $\epsilon_G:QR(G)\to G$ by sheafification. It is locally surjective: for $g\in G(T)$ apply step 2 to its image in $X(T)$ to choose local $x_i$, and use $\eta([i,(x_i,g)])$. It is injective on sections: if $f,f^{\prime}$ have the same image $g$, represent them on a common covering by $[i,(x_i,g)]$ and $[j,(x_j,g)]$ using the cited local-representation lemma and the composition/base-change axioms for coverings. These two representatives are related by the canonical transition, hence have equal classes, so $f=f^{\prime}$ by the sheaf axiom. Local preimages now agree on overlaps by injectivity and glue, proving surjectivity on every $T$. Thus $\epsilon_G$ is an isomorphism over $X$; it is natural in $G$ by its formula on representatives and the uniqueness in sheafification.

source.place: Tag 0ADT (lemma-descent-data-sheaves), coequalizer construction and verification of the quasi-inverses

proof.text: The natural isomorphisms in steps 7 and 8 make $Q$ and $R$ quasi-inverse. Explicitly, given compatible maps $h_i:X_i\times_XG\to X_i\times_XH$, sheafify their map on quotient representatives as in step 7 and compose with $\epsilon_G^{-1}$ and $\epsilon_H$. Its pullback is $h_i$ by the formula on representatives. Conversely two maps $G\to H$ with the same pullbacks agree on each section after the covering from step 2, and then agree by the sheaf axiom for $H$. This gives the asserted bijection on maps and the equivalence, including the displayed local identifications of step 7. Empty families cause no exception: an empty family covers only the empty $X$, and all local existence and equality arguments use the empty covering and its sheaf axiom. No atlas or representable diagonal for the resulting global $F$ was used or asserted.

Step-by-step checks: steps 1-2 use the fibre-product lemma and covering calculus (2),(3),(1),(4) for local lifting; schemes are treated as algebraic spaces, the DAG's standing convention. Step 3 builds the transports: τ_ii is the identity from the (i,i,i) cocycle and bijectivity, τ_ji=τ_ij^{-1} from (i,j,i), and the relation is an equivalence stable under restriction. Step 4 takes F=P^{++} with p:F→X. Step 5 proves injectivity from the local-equality clause of lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local plus τ_ii=id. Step 6 proves surjectivity through w_a=τ_{j_a i}(v_a), gluing by step 5. Step 7 recovers exactly φ_ij (I traced (v_i,x_j) through both sides) and builds the functor Q. Step 8: the counit is well defined, locally surjective via step 2 (the only use of the covering hypothesis, which is right) and injective via the canonical τ. Step 9 assembles the quasi-inverses. Edge cases: identity cover, repeated members, I=∅ (only X=∅; sheafification gives the one section over ∅), and empty V_i. reviewed_lean.note: The descent category's natural transport on generalized points is equivalent by Yoneda to the overlap isomorphisms φij with the cocycle (self+cocycle give invertibility; invertible φ with the cocycle gives self).
